query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a controlled amount of Ti and refinement of grain size through mechanical alloying can overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, leading to improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Introduction of a controlled amount of Ti and refinement of grain size through mechanical alloying
generation.conditions: Target density below 6 g/cm3, room temperature, and exposure to air or corrosive environments
generation.structural_mediator: Refined grain size and Ti-induced solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: Ti addition strengthens the alloy and increases its ability to withstand extremes of temperature, while grain refinement enhances mechanical properties and corrosion resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
generation.boundary: Alloy composition: Mg and other principal elements with individual atomic concentrations ranging from 5% to 35%; Temperature: room temperature to high temperatures; Exposure time: short-term to long-term; Test environment: air or corrosive environments
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Ti to be introduced and the optimal grain size refinement technique are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with varying amounts of Ti and grain sizes, and test their room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of Ti and refinement of grain size do not lead to significant improvements in room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation, the hypothesis is falsified
